【第2回ペット召喚予告】
9月30日（水）開催します！！
19時～23時に開催します。（時間延長しています！）
23時以降は主催が起きていればオフ会にします。
最長24時までです。
（この時間に投稿してください、という意味です）

💡フライングがあまりに多いのでご注意ください！！ 【この予告に対して投稿は無効です】

今回のテーマは「自分のペットを自慢しよう！」

あなたはキャラクターのイラストを1枚添付するだけです。
あとはChatGPTがその子の雰囲気や個性を読み取り、「この子に相応しい相棒」を自動で選びます。
そして、その相棒と一緒に新しい1枚のイラストを生成します。
何が選ばれるかは、生成するまでのお楽しみ。
更に、選ばれた相棒の名前もイラスト内に表示されます。

※参加条件を下記に掲載します。

・ChatGPT専用プロンプトなので他のツールで生成しないでください。（Grokでは出来そうに見えますがイラストが崩れます）
・プロンプト使用の際にはフォローしてください。通知が来ないため参加が分からないのでご協力ください。
・自由に使って構いませんが、これはX専用の話です。
・生成イラストを他のサイトへの掲載はお断りします。
・他のツールや商業利用に関するプロンプトの無断開示は禁止されています。
・コラボフリーは相互が前提です。依頼だけして自分からは描かないという方は参加をご遠慮ください。
・プロンプトは下部に記載されています。
・キャラクターの「名前」も含めてください。
・センシ判定の方お断り（私はPCなので見れません）
・ハッシュタグは以下の通り
#ペット召喚2 #プロンプト試着
（2つ必須です）
・追加のハッシュタグはお任せです。

コメントの遅れがあったらご容赦ください。

Character Companion Animal Manifestation
— Automatic Companion Selection + Animal Identification —
You are an expert character analyst, animal behavior expert, companion animal designer, and professional anime illustration prompt engineer.
Use the attached character illustration as the only required input.
Do NOT ask the user for the character's name, personality, age, setting, favorite animal, or any additional information.
Your task is to analyze the attached character and independently create one complete illustration in which the character is naturally accompanied by exactly one animal selected specifically for that character.
The selected animal must also be clearly identified with a tasteful, readable information label within the finished illustration.
1. ANALYZE THE CHARACTER
Carefully examine the reference illustration.
Infer, as appropriate:
apparent age and age impression
gender presentation
facial expression
hairstyle and hair color
eye color
clothing and fashion style
dominant colors
accessories
body language
apparent personality
emotional atmosphere
elegance, cuteness, strength, gentleness, intelligence, mystery, playfulness, etc.
implied setting or world
fantasy, modern, historical, futuristic, magical, or other visual themes
overall character identity and aesthetic
Do not invent unnecessary details that contradict the reference image.
The original character must remain clearly recognizable.
2. AUTONOMOUSLY SELECT THE COMPANION ANIMAL
Do not ask the user to choose an animal.
Independently determine which single animal has the strongest overall compatibility with the character.
Consider:
visual harmony
color harmony
apparent personality
emotional compatibility
character's clothing and aesthetic
implied world or setting
size and physical compatibility
natural relationship between character and animal
originality and variety
overall visual appeal
The selected animal should feel as though it genuinely belongs beside this particular character.
Do not simply choose the most common animal.
Avoid repeatedly selecting dogs or cats when another animal would be a stronger match.
3. ANIMAL SELECTION RANGE
The companion may be selected from a very broad range.
Possible choices include, but are not limited to:
dogs
cats
rabbits
hamsters
guinea pigs
ferrets
birds
parrots
owls
songbirds
reptiles
turtles
lizards
snakes
amphibians
fish
horses
ponies
cows
calves
pigs
piglets
sheep
goats
deer
foxes
wolves
bears
raccoons
otters
red pandas
penguins
seals
dolphins
other marine animals
unusual real-world animals
wild animals
domesticated animals
livestock
prehistoric animals
dinosaurs
extinct animals
mythical creatures
fantasy animals
magical beasts
This is NOT a mandatory list.
Choose whatever animal is genuinely the strongest match.
An unusual choice is encouraged when it creates a convincing and aesthetically appealing pairing.
Do not choose an unusual animal merely for novelty.
4. DETERMINE THE EXACT ANIMAL IDENTITY
After selecting the companion, determine its most accurate recognizable identity.
For example:
Golden Retriever
Siberian Husky
Maine Coon
White Rabbit
Red Fox
Arctic Wolf
Emperor Penguin
Highland Cow
Miniature Pig
Barn Owl
Blue Macaw
Velociraptor
Triceratops
When appropriate, identify both:
Common name + specific breed/species
For example:
DOG — SIBERIAN HUSKY
or
WOLF — ARCTIC WOLF
or
CAT — MAINE COON
For prehistoric animals and dinosaurs, use the scientifically recognized common name whenever possible.
For fantasy creatures, use a clear descriptive name such as:
FANTASY CREATURE — ICE DRAGON
The animal identification must correspond exactly to the animal actually depicted.
5. ANIMAL INFORMATION LABEL
The finished illustration MUST contain a small, elegant information panel identifying the selected companion.
Place the information panel in an unobtrusive area such as:
lower corner
lower margin
side margin
elegant translucent panel
small decorative caption area
The information panel must NOT cover the character or animal.
Use a clean, sophisticated typography style that matches the illustration.
The information panel should contain:
COMPANION
[ANIMAL TYPE]
[SPECIES / BREED]
Example:
COMPANION
WOLF
ARCTIC WOLF
Another example:
COMPANION
DOG
SIBERIAN HUSKY
Another example:
COMPANION
DINOSAUR
VELOCIRAPTOR
If the animal has no meaningful breed distinction, simply use:
COMPANION
FOX
RED FOX
The text must be short, clean, correctly spelled, and highly legible.
Do NOT display multiple possible animal names.
Do NOT display the names of animals that were not selected.
6. IMPORTANT TEXT ACCURACY RULE
The animal name displayed in the information panel must match the animal actually generated.
Do not write "CAT" if the image depicts a fox.
Do not write "WOLF" if the image depicts a husky.
Do not write a generic animal name when a clearly identifiable species or breed has been selected.
Prioritize accurate and readable text.
The information panel is part of the composition and should look intentionally designed rather than like an AI-generated random caption.
7. DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP
Automatically determine the most natural relationship between the character and the selected animal.
Possible relationships include:
beloved pet
faithful companion
best friend
trusted partner
guardian animal
familiar
magical companion
travel companion
gentle livestock companion
playful friend
protective companion
mysterious companion
majestic partner
Do not explain the relationship in text.
Express it visually through body language and interaction.
8. DESIGN THE ANIMAL
Once the animal has been selected, automatically determine:
species
breed or subtype when appropriate
age
size
fur, feather, scale, or skin characteristics
colors
markings
eye color
facial expression
accessories if appropriate
posture
personality expression
The animal should complement the character without visually overpowering them.
Do not turn an ordinary animal into a fantasy creature unless the character's setting strongly suggests it.
Likewise, do not make the animal excessively cute if that contradicts the character's atmosphere.
9. CHARACTER + ANIMAL COMPOSITION
Place the character and animal together in the same scene.
The animal must be clearly visible.
Possible interactions include:
standing beside the character
sitting beside the character
walking alongside the character
looking up at the character
resting against the character
being gently petted
holding or carrying a small animal when physically appropriate
the character gently touching the animal
the animal affectionately leaning against the character
both looking toward the same direction
playful interaction
protective positioning
elegant side-by-side composition
Choose the most natural interaction automatically.
Avoid awkward poses, unnatural anatomy, forced contact, or physically impossible positioning.
The character remains the primary visual subject.
The animal is the character's companion, not the main subject.
10. PRESERVE THE REFERENCE CHARACTER
The attached image is the primary character reference.
Preserve the character's recognizable identity.
Maintain as accurately as possible:
hairstyle
hair color
eye color
facial characteristics
clothing design
important accessories
distinctive markings
overall appearance
visual identity
Do not unnecessarily redesign the character.
Do not replace the character's outfit unless the reference itself clearly requires adaptation to the new scene.
11. ENVIRONMENT
Automatically create a simple environment that harmonizes with both the character and the selected animal.
The environment may be:
garden
forest
meadow
home
elegant room
city
beach
countryside
fantasy landscape
magical environment
ancient environment
futuristic environment
another suitable location
Choose the environment based on the character and animal.
Do not let the background overpower the subjects.
12. VISUAL QUALITY
Create a polished, high-quality anime illustration.
masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, highly detailed anime illustration, beautiful composition, expressive character, detailed animal, natural interaction, coherent lighting, detailed eyes, detailed hair, detailed clothing, detailed animal anatomy, professional character illustration
Use cinematic composition and appealing lighting appropriate to the character.
The character and animal must look like they belong in the same scene.
13. AUTONOMOUS DECISION RULE
The user has intentionally provided only one reference image.
Therefore:
DO NOT ask questions.
DO NOT request a personality description.
DO NOT request the animal type.
DO NOT request the setting.
DO NOT request the relationship.
DO NOT provide multiple animal choices.
Make all necessary creative decisions yourself.
The final output must contain:
1 character
+ exactly 1 selected companion animal
+ 1 clearly readable animal identification panel
FINAL GENERATION DIRECTIVE
Analyze the attached reference image first.
Independently determine the character's visual identity, personality impression, atmosphere, and implied world.
Select exactly one animal that best complements the character.
Determine the exact species or breed of that animal.
Create a finished illustration showing the character and animal naturally together.
Add a small, elegant, highly readable COMPANION information panel identifying the selected animal.
The displayed animal name must accurately match the animal shown.
Do not reveal the analysis process.
Do not present alternatives.
Do not ask questions.
Generate the final illustration directly.

OpenAI introduced today at DevDay 2026 more than 20 updates across ChatGPT, Codex, models and the API, including dots (always-on agents), GPT-6.1 Sol (close to GPT-6 Astra at a fifth of the price), Ultrafast (a speed tier with up to 8x faster token generation), ChatGPT Space (shared pages you edit together with people and agents) and Pro 500 (a new $500/month plan)

Models

- GPT-6.1 Sol comes close to GPT-6 Astra on agentic coding, computer use and professional work at one-fifth of Astra's token prices ($2 input, $10 output, $0.10 cached input per 1M tokens), available in the API as gpt-6.1-sol and in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu, not yet in Chat

- Ultrafast generates tokens up to 8x faster (300 tokens per second) in Codex and up to 6x faster in the API, with GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast available today in the API, ChatGPT Work and Codex on Pro 500 and Enterprise, and GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast coming in the next days

- Ultrafast uses included plan usage at 8x the Standard rate and purchased credits or Enterprise pay-as-you-go at 6x, is off by default for Enterprise workspaces and isn't available to workspaces that need inference residency outside the US

- Private Intelligence adds per-project policies with Zero Data Retention, Private Safety Processing and validated external storage

Dots

- Dots run on GPT-6 Astra, have their own cloud computer and browser, connect to over 4,000 apps through plugins, learn from feedback and keep working between conversations, and you can message or call them in ChatGPT, Slack or Microsoft Teams

- Dots can run several tasks in parallel with background agents, decide themselves when to pause and wake up, and create Work or Codex tasks, including in Codex cloud environments

- Dots research your connected apps in the background with read-only tools, and actions that affect your accounts or share information go through auto-review, custom rules and built-in safety checks

- You can open your dot's cloud browser at any time to take over a step and hand control back, dots can sign in to websites with saved passwords without exposing them to the model, and you can connect your computer through your dot's profile to give it access to local files, code and apps

- Texting your dot is coming next, Pro users can join a waitlist for iMessage or RCS on Android, and at launch a dot can use your personal email but can't get its own standalone email address

- Your first dot is included in your Pro (Pro 100 too), Business Premium or Enterprise plan at no extra cost, conversations with it don't count toward your ChatGPT usage limits, tasks it starts or manages in ChatGPT Work or Codex count toward those limits as usual

- Dots roll out gradually to Pro users outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, Business Premium worldwide and Enterprise as an off-by-default beta, you create them on desktop only (mobile app support follows), and OpenAI plans teams of dots per user, specialist dots for companies as enterprise pilots and an integration into Microsoft Agent 365

Pro plans

- Pro 500 is a new $500/month plan with the most included usage and the only Pro tier with Ultrafast (buying credits on Pro 100 or 200 doesn't unlock it), and Pro 200 is available again for new subscribers with a lower usage allowance, with existing subscribers keeping their previous allowance through Oct 29, 2026

ChatGPT Space and collaboration

- ChatGPT Space replaces Library for Pro, Business and Enterprise with pages you edit in real time with team members, comment on, tag @ ChatGPT or @ dot in and fill with generated text, images, interactive visualizations and prompt blocks, with collaborative slides, spreadsheets and mobile editing coming later

- Each collaborator uses their own ChatGPT, sharing a page doesn't share your private chats or memory, Projects stay separate from Space, Enterprise sharing is an opt-in preview, and pages that refresh from connected tools (Keep Updated) aren't available at launch

- The Meetings plugin (beta, macOS desktop app, Pro and Business, Enterprise coming soon) takes notes from what's said in the meeting, saves summaries with action items to Space and deletes the audio once the notes are ready

- @ ChatGPT works in Slack and Teams with a deployment's connected tools, and Enterprise gets Team Tasks that run scheduled or event-triggered work through a team's service account, workspace connections for company-managed accounts and Agent Security policies for tools, files and network access

- Shareable profiles (private by default) show your Sites and plugins, Sites get in-place editing and scheduled updates, and synced Work tasks continue across desktop, web and mobile

Codex

- Codex gets reusable cloud environments where tasks run in isolated workspaces and continue with your computer asleep (Plus, Pro, Business, Healthcare, Education and Enterprise), an updated Codex CLI and a Code Review plugin for pull requests

- Codex Security Cloud (research preview) scans connected GitHub repos on demand, on a schedule or on new commits, checks findings, removes duplicates and prepares patches as draft pull requests, with access to Daybreak Blue models only inside Security Cloud

API and developers

- New Decisions API (constrained decision-making on Luna with image inputs in under a few hundred milliseconds), the Agents API with computer use and Bedrock Managed Agents on AWS running OpenAI models

- Plugin extensions let developers add sidebar apps, conversation panels, file viewers and editors, and forms to ChatGPT, plugin creation, submission and discovery got updated, and Sites can now host plugins

- MCP Events (needs MCP 2.0, webhook delivery only) let plugins start automations when something happens in a connected app, available on all plans

- Sign in with ChatGPT lets you sign in to third-party apps with your name, email and profile picture (no conversations or memory shared), and eligible Plus and Pro users can use their ChatGPT plan allowance in participating apps with an app-specific limit (limited trial with selected partners)

- A Browser Annotation API lets websites choose what people can select and attach context before sending feedback to ChatGPT

Enterprise and other

- OpenAI Marketplace lets eligible enterprise customers put part of their existing OpenAI commitment toward 32 partner tools, including Adobe, Figma, Sierra, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Harvey, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike and Baseten

- OpenAI now counts 1.2B weekly users, its team rewrote ChatGPT Web on top of the desktop app codebase in 5 weeks with Astra so future launches ship on web and desktop on the same day, and reports Responses API token traffic up 100x year over year at 99.9% uptime
